newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 15.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 15.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Tuesday:
* The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 1.16 points at 7,922.98 on Monday as blue-chips closed slightly higher, but the Nasdaq market soared as technology stocks extending their powerful rally.

* Indonesia's central bank governor and the Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor said they would cooperate closely in financial markets when they discussed Asian currency markets in a meeting on Monday afternoon, Takashi Anzai, BOJ executive director, told reporters.
* On Tuesday, the Indonesian rupiah continued to recover against the dollar in early trading after previously sliding on regional turbulence, dealers said.
* The Indonesian central bank said fundamentals were stronger than portrayed by the media.

* Jakarta stocks ended down on Monday as overall market sentiment remained cautious as regional currency volatility spilled over to the rupiah. The Jakarta composite index ended down 0.92 points, or 0.13 percent, at 722.50 points.
* On Tuesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,450.00/5.00 at 0215 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,455.00/2,465.00.

* Conglomerate Bakrie & Brothers following a report which quoted drug maker and distributor Inovax Ltd in Sydney as saying a consortium led by the Bakrie Group was expected to have majority control of the company once an acquisition was completed later this calendar year.

* Banking stocks following the government decision to limit loans for land purchase and development. Also after Moody's Investors Service said it was revising its ratings outlook for Indonesia's state banks to uncertain from stable pending a decision on planned mergers among the seven institutions.
* Fishery firm Daya Guna Samudera after a news report that the government had revoked import duty on fish caught in Indonesia's exclusive economic zone.
* Cement maker Semen Gresik on market talk it might acquire another state-owned cement firm.

* Indonesian petrochemical company PT GT Petrochem Industries ADMG.JKL, a member of the Gajah Tunggal Group, said on Monday a wholly-owned subsidiary GTPI Netherlands B.V. had signed a $300 million syndicated term loan facility with 22 financial institutions. The firm said the loan would be used to strengthen its financial performance and expand production.
* Cement maker PT Indocement and its sister company noodle maker PT Indofood Sukses Makmur on continued market talk that Indocement would divest its stake in Indofood.

* Small-capitalised metals firm PT Alumindo Light Metal Industries on a report that the International Finance Corporation, a World Bank unit, said it would provide loans worth $35 million to fund the firm's expansion plans.
